fields.reasoning: The change set's intent prescribes this fix. Abandoning a run is the owner's (or orchestrator's) explicit dismissal, and a withdrawn or rejected change set has nothing left to recover, so a hold on either is an inbox item nobody can act on and no command clears. Recomputing holds from journals and change-set states each poll needs no migration or prune step for holds already saved.
fields.statement: A watchdog hold lasts only while its run can still be acted on: a run that is abandoned, or whose change set is withdrawn or rejected, gets no hold, and since holds are recomputed each poll its existing hold is gone at the next poll

fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath ./internal/api -run 'TestWatchdog(Budget|Holds)' covers a run with its retry budget spent that is then abandoned, and one whose change set is withdrawn and one rejected: each poll after leaves no hold for it in the daemon state and inbox shows no stalled item for it, while a spent-budget failed run that is not abandoned keeps its one hold
fields.statement: The watchdog keeps no hold, and rhiza inbox lists no watchdog item, for a run that is abandoned or whose change set is withdrawn or rejected; a hold saved for such a run before is dropped at the next poll
